overview_markdown:
Loong is a Rust-based foundation for building vertical AI agents, positioning itself as an architecture-first alternative in the OpenClaw-adjacent ecosystem. Its core design principle is **architecture-governed safety**: outbound effects are modeled as `Action`s that must be authorized by policy before execution, with sandboxes and model review serving as defense-in-depth rather than the primary boundary.

The project is built on a custom Actor runtime (`loac` / `loac-macros`) with a well-defined lifetime model, making components easy to run, stop, restart, and extend. Recent commits show active refinement of the message-handling API — converging on `Handler`/`StreamHandler` shapes, adding a `SyncHandler` for ready replies, and building agents from serializable `AgentConfig`. Extensibility is planned along two paths: compile-time Rust integrations for performance-sensitive work, and runtime-loaded scripts for faster iteration, both under the same security expectations.

Critically, Loong is transparent about its maturity: this is an independent-history rewrite that currently contains an architecture and contract skeleton, **not a usable agent product**. Unlike OpenClaw's massive ecosystem of channels, skills, and a control UI, Loong offers no end-user functionality yet. It is best understood as a bet on a secure, evolvable Rust core that may grow into a serious OpenClaw alternative — worth watching and contributing to, but not deploying today.
